body.statement: Throughout the low-intensity regime, \(\exp(-\kappa m_*)L\{1-\alpha\exp(\kappa\overline m_*)\}\le D_{\mathrm{rand}}(\kappa)\le(1-\alpha)L<D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)\), with the left side truncated below at zero. Moreover, as \(\kappa\downarrow0\), \(D_{\mathrm{rand}}(\kappa)\to(1-\alpha)L\), \(D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)\to L\), and \(D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)-D_{\mathrm{rand}}(\kappa)\to\alpha L\).
body.justification: This isolates randomization as a first-order decision resource at the zero-information boundary rather than as a numerical convenience.
body.gap: Kabaila (2013) shows atom splitting for scalar binomial tails; no located result proves strict minimax improvement in this staggered multivariate Poisson nuisance game.
body.consumer: Regulators and analysts can quantify the exact price of forbidding auxiliary randomization when sparse counts make one table dominate coverage.
